<div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?forumId=1&comments_parentId=5719&comments_per_page=1&thread_style=commentStyle_plain Zendo In Lojban]</div><br></div><div><div>Posted by Anonymous on Wed 07 of Dec., 2005 14:55 GMT</div><div>
On 12/7/05, Robin Lee Powell wrote: 
> On Wed, Dec 07, 2005 at 09:28:43AM -0300, Jorge Llamb?as wrote: 
> > BTW, I think {gunma} means "consists of", not "contains". The x2 
> > of gunma are all the constituents of x1. There's {selpau} or 
> > {selcmi} or {vasru} for "contains". 
> 
> "contains" in Zendo doesn't really mean "contains"; gunma was 
> suggested by kpreid, and it's really much better.

I take {gunma pa xunre dacti} to mean "consists of exactly one 
red piece", no other pieces of any kind. In other words, I take 
{gunma} to mean what you use {mulgunma} for. In other words, 
if a koan ko'a consists of ko'e and ko'i, I would say:

ko'a gunma koe joi ko'i 
"ko'a consists of ko'e and ko'i together"

and not

ko'a gunma ko'e .e ko'i

Which to me does not mean "ko'a contains ko'e and ko'a contains 
ko'i" but "ko'a consists of ko'e" and at the asme time "ko'a consists 
of ko'i", which would only make sense if ko'e and ko'i are the same 
things.

mu'o mi'e xorxes
</div></div></div><div><div>'''Score''': 0.00 '''Vote''': <div> 1  2  3  4  5 </div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?comments_parentId=5713&topics_offset=162&topics_sort_mode=lastPost_desc&forumId=1#tiki-top [[Archivo:resultset_up.png|16px|top of page]]]</div><div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?comments_parentId=5713&topics_offset=162&topics_sort_mode=lastPost_desc&forumId=1&post_reply=1&comments_threshold=0&comments_reply_threadId=5719&comments_offset=0&thread_sort_mode=commentDate_asc&comments_per_page=300&comments_grandParentId=5713&thread_style=commentStyle_plain#form Reply]</div></div><br></div></div><div><div><div><div><div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?forumId=1&comments_threadId=5720&comments_threshold=0&comments_offset=0&thread_sort_mode=commentDate_asc&comments_per_page=300&comments_parentId=5713&thread_style=commentStyle_plain&edit_reply=1#form [[Archivo:page_edit.png|16px|Edit]]] [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?forumId=1&comments_threshold=0&comments_threadId=5720&comments_remove=1&comments_offset=0&thread_sort_mode=commentDate_asc&comments_per_page=300&comments_parentId=5713&thread_style=commentStyle_plain [[Archivo:cross.png|16px|Delete]]] [http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?comments_parentId=5713&topics_offset=162&topics_sort_mode=lastPost_desc&forumId=1&report=5720 [[Archivo:delete.png|16px|Report this post]]]

> > Then you need to take that up with the gismu list. Everyone on 
> > IRC at the time I asked (except me) said that the x2 of gunma 
> > need not be a complete specification. 
> 
> If it's not a complete specification, the "considered jointly" 
> does not make a lot of sense.

I don't see a strong connection there.

{ly ly gy gunma mi joi la xorxes}, for example; is certainly true 
that the LLG consists of you and I, considered jointly, but that is 
not *all* it consists of.

For the record, I agree with you; when about 3 people all disagreed 
with me simultaneously, I decided that that was clearly not the only 
reading of the gismu list.

The problem with "vasru" is that a koan is not a container in any 
obvious sense. Do you have any suggestions for a more specific way 
to get at the "contains some things including X" without "joi lo 
drata" ?

> > > if a koan ko'a consists of ko'e and ko'i, I would say: 
> > > 
> > > ko'a gunma ko'e joi ko'i 
> > > 
> > > "ko'a consists of ko'e and ko'i together" 
> > > 
> > > and not 
> > > 
> > > ko'a gunma ko'e .e ko'i 
> > 
> > You are, of course, correct that me usage of .e is wrong. Hardly 
> > the first time. [[Archivo:icon_smile.gif|:-)]] 
> > 
> > That doesn't mean that the x2 of gunma is a full specification, 
> > though. Seperate issues. 
> 
> Not a separate issue. If a mere component is enough in x2, then 
> the {.e} version is perfectly correct, since each of {ko'a gunma 
> ko'e} and {ko'a gunma ko'i} would be true.

Yeah, I eventually realized that.

-Robin

<div>[http://www.lojban.org/tiki/tiki-view_forum_thread.php?forumId=1&comments_parentId=5723&comments_per_page=1&thread_style=commentStyle_plain Zendo In Lojban]</div><br></div><div><div>Posted by Anonymous on Wed 07 of Dec., 2005 16:54 GMT</div><div>
On 12/7/05, Robin Lee Powell wrote: 
> {ly ly gy gunma mi joi la xorxes}, for example; is certainly true 
> that the LLG consists of you and I, considered jointly, but that is 
> not *all* it consists of.

We have a different understanding of "consist of" then, I would not 
say in English that the LLG consists of you and I.

> For the record, I agree with you; when about 3 people all disagreed 
> with me simultaneously, I decided that that was clearly not the only 
> reading of the gismu list.

I don't see what the "considered jointly" adds to the definition if 
the LLG can "consist of you" and at the same time "consist of me".

> The problem with "vasru" is that a koan is not a container in any 
> obvious sense. Do you have any suggestions for a more specific way 
> to get at the "contains some things including X" without "joi lo 
> drata" ?

{selcmi}. {ko'a selcmi ko'e} says that ko'a contains ko'e in the 
required sense (not as a separate container) without saying 
whether or not it contains anything else.

{selpau} would also work, except it would seem to require there 
to be at least some other part, i.e. {ko'a selpau ko'e} says that 
ko'e is part of ko'a, but there would have to be some other parts 
to ko'a besides ko'e.

I can't really vouch for any of this of course. I can only 
tell you how I interpret these words.

mu'o mi'e xorxes

One also speaks of the human visual field as having "2 and a half" dimensions, because the binocular vision *sorta* gives us some third-dimension. This is also unrelated to fractal dimensionality, which doesn't really enter into this.

Zendo blocks are definitely 3-dimensional. You even describe them as having planar faces and a "hollow" *face* on the bottom. That they are empty doesn't really enter into things. They're 3D blocks, and are treated as such in the game. (Also a little as containers, which is another matter.)
